discovery: The self-amplified spontaneous emission (SASE) X-ray free-electron laser

nominees.name: Claudio Pellegrini
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Kwang-Je Kim
nominees.affiliation: Argonne National Laboratory and University of Chicago, USA

motivation: The nominees laid the theoretical and conceptual foundations of the high-gain, self-amplified spontaneous emission free-electron laser and showed how it could reach hard X-ray wavelengths. Pellegrini proposed using a high-brightness linac to drive an angstrom-wavelength SASE FEL, the idea realised at LCLS in 2009. Kim developed the theory of start-up from noise, transverse coherence and gain in the high-gain regime. Saldin, with DESY colleagues, made the quantitative theory and design that underpinned FLASH and European XFEL, and introduced self-seeding concepts. The result is a new kind of light source, a billion times brighter than synchrotrons, with femtosecond pulses. It has opened ultrafast structural biology, nonlinear X-ray optics, matter under extreme conditions and time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of electronic dynamics. Facilities now operate in the USA, Germany, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and China, serving thousands of users across physics, chemistry and biology.
